question: For a potential stop condition on a 55-mph approach, what advance placement distance is shown in Table 2C-3, and should it be treated as an inflexible mandatory distance?
model_answer: Direct Answer: For a potential stop condition (Condition B, deceleration to 0 mph — the column keyed to Stop Ahead, Yield Ahead, Signal Ahead, and Intersection Warning signs), Table 2C-3 shows an advance placement distance of 495 feet for a 55-mph posted or 85th-percentile speed. No — the distance is not an inflexible mandate: the table is expressly titled "Guidelines," and Section 2C.04 (Guidance) states the distances should be applied with engineering judgment. What is mandatory is the installation of an Advance Traffic Control sign where the primary device is not visible for a sufficient distance, and, at passive grade crossings, that the Stop/Yield Ahead sign be located in accordance with Table 2C-3. Standards (mandatory): - "The Stop Ahead (W3-1), Yield Ahead (W3-2), and Signal Ahead (W3-3) Advance Traffic Control signs (see Figure 2C-8) shall be installed on an approach to a primary traffic control device that is not visible for a sufficient distance to permit the road user to respond to the device (see Table 2C-3)." - At passive grade crossings with a YIELD or STOP sign: "The Yield Ahead or Stop Ahead sign shall be located in accordance with Table 2C-3. The minimum distance between the signs shall be in accordance with Section 2C.04 and Table 2C-3." Guidance (recommended): - Table 2C-3 ("Guidelines for Advance Placement of Warning Signs") lists 495 ft for the 55-mph row under Condition B, deceleration to 0 mph — the "potential stop" condition (footnote 3: Stop Ahead, Yield Ahead, Signal Ahead, and Intersection Warning signs, based on stopping sight distance with a PRT of 2.5 seconds and a deceleration rate of 11.2 ft/s²). - Per the table's footnote 1, for warning signs with less than 6-inch legend or more than four words, a minimum of 100 feet should be added to the advance placement distance to provide adequate legibility. - Section 2C.04 frames the table as guidance to be evaluated and applied with judgment: "The effectiveness of the placement of warning signs should be periodically evaluated under both day and night conditions." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Table 2C-3 shows the 55 mph row with 495 ft in the "0³" (potential stop) column under Condition B, and footnote 3 explaining the potential-stop basis. - [Image 2] The full page of Section 2C.04 shows the Guidance provisions that warning signs "should be placed so that they provide an adequate PRT" and that "the distances contained in Table 2C-3 should be applied with engineering judgment," confirming the distances are recommended, not mandatory. - [Image 3] Figure 2C-13 (Sheet 5) directs users to "See Table 2C-3 to determine the advance placement distance," illustrating the table's role as a placement aid. - [Image 4] Figure 2C-13 (Sheet 1) similarly annotates the sign location with "See Table 2C-3 to determine the advance placement distance." - [Image 5] Figure 2C-2 notes "See Table 2C-3 for advance placement distance guidelines," reinforcing the table's guideline (not mandatory) character. Citations: - Table 2C-3 (p.152) - Section 2C.04 Guidance §804 (p.153) - Section 2C.04 Guidance §5 (p.152) - Section 2C.35 Standard §1 (p.177) - Section 8B.06 Standard §3 (p.1001) - Page 193 - Page 230 - Page 226 - Page 197
gold_answer: The table shows 495 feet. It is a guideline to be applied with engineering judgment and may be adjusted for roadway features, other signing, and visibility; it is not an inflexible universal mandate.
